strong_form: 12 divisions of the octave are favored because log2(3) ≈ 19/12 (2^(19/12) ≈ 2.9966, about 2 cents from 3), equivalently 2^(7/12) ≈ 3/2; 7/12 is a continued-fraction convergent of log2(3/2), so 12 is the smallest equal division that gives a near-pure fifth with a manageable number of notes.
weak_form: The arithmetic coincidence 2^19 ≈ 3^12 (Pythagorean comma ≈ 23.5 cents) is what lets 12-tone equal temperament close the circle of fifths with tiny error.
refuted_if: 2^(19/12) differing materially from 3 (it does not: 2.99661), or showing that 12-TET's adoption and success are better explained by something unrelated to fifth approximation (e.g., if smaller/other divisions approximated fifths equally well and were rejected for reasons of fifths).

prior_art.citation: Harmony and Duality: An introduction to Music Theory, arXiv:2309.10719
Why the Kirnberger Kernel Is So Small, arXiv:0907.5249 (12-note scale as coincidence of 3 ≈ 2^(19/12))

strongest_criticism: The arithmetic is exact and well known, but 'works because' is only half the story. 12-TET also depends on 2^(4/12) roughly approximating 5/4 (the major third, about 14 cents sharp), which matters for triadic harmony, and on a historical path running through meantone and well temperaments to keyboard practicality. The fact is standard textbook material in tuning theory, stated in many explainers.
